{{Quote|That was when I went with a relief group to Shadda-Bi-Boran. Their sun was imploding and the planet was dying. I was helping to relocate the children.|Padmé Amidala, explaining a holograph of her younger self to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="AOTC novel">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>}}
'''Shadda-Bi-Boran''' was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] inhabited by a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of the [[Shadda-Bi-Boran (species)|same name]]. It had three [[Moon/Legends|moons]] and contained plains and [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]]. Shadda-Bi-Boran [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] the [[Star/Legends|sun]] [[Shadda (star)|Shadda]], which had reached its [[White dwarf/Legends|white dwarf]] phase by the decline of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The resulting implosion threatened the Shadda-Bi-Borans, who had a purifying enzyme only activated by Shadda's sunlight.

Fundraising and research efforts throughout the [[galactic community]] to find a substitute for the Shadda-Bi-Borans' enzyme or a suitable new star failed. In [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]], as Shadda-Bi-Boran began to [[Temperature/Legends|freeze]] over, the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]] sent volunteers to evacuate the population in the hope that some distant planets would have appropriate conditions for the species. The final Shadda-Bi-Borans were evacuated as the planet froze, and ultimately the species was unable to adapt elsewhere and went [[Death/Legends|extinct]].

==Description==
Shadda-Bi-Boran was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Shadda-Bi-Boran system]] of the [[Bi-Boran Cluster]],<ref name="TEA" /> a part of the [[Toblain sector/Legends|Toblain sector]]<ref name="TEA appendix" /> in the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. The planet had three [[Moon/Legends|moons]] and held the second [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] position around the [[Star/Legends|sun]] [[Shadda (star)|Shadda]]. A [[Local day/Legends|day]] on Shadda-Bi-Boran lasted sixteen [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]], while a [[local year]] lasted 271 days. The planet had a diameter of 9,100 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]], and its surface featured plains and [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]].<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
{{Quote|They were never able to adapt, they were never able to live off their native planet.|Padmé Amidala, on the Shadda-Bi-Borans|<ref name="AOTC novel" />}}
The [[Shadda-Bi-Boran (species)|Shadda-Bi-Borans]] were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the planet of the same name. The species developed a [[Poison/Legends|toxin]]-cleansing enzyme activated by the [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]] from Shadda's sunlight. Eons before the final [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Shadda transformed from a [[Red giant/Legends|red giant]] into a [[White dwarf/Legends|white dwarf]], a process that led to cataclysmic weather events and major [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquakes]] on Shadda-Bi-Boran. [[Astrophysicist/Legends|Astrophysicists]] eventually predicted that Shadda would soon cease to generate enough radiation to prevent Shadda-Bi-Boran from [[Temperature/Legends|freezing]] over and releasing its [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] into [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Na-kee-tula.png|thumb|right|250px|Padmé Naberrie (center) alongside two Shadda-Bi-Boran children during the planet's evacuation effort]]
The Shadda-Bi-Borans were initally unable to be evacuated from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] due to their dependence on Shadda's light. Kerchiefs made of [[Shadda silk]] were sold throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], with the proceeds divided between researching a substitute for the enzyme and finding another star that matched Shadda's characteristics. In [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]], the planet's [[Death/Legends|death]] became final<ref name="TEA" /> as Shadda imploded,<ref name="AOTC novel" /> and volunteers from the [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]], among them the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Naberrie]], arrived on Shadda-Bi-Boran. They intended to [[Shadda-Bi-Boran exodus|evacuate]] the population in the hope that some distant stars would give rise to suitable planetary conditions for the species. However, none survived. A final [[Refugee/Legends|refugee]] [[Starship/Legends|ship]] carrying one hundred Shadda-Bi-Borans departed the planet as it froze over. Upon hearing that the rest of their species had died, the survivors refused pleas to go into stasis or [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|carbon-freezing]], and all had perished within [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of the demise of their planet.<ref name="TEA" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> while traveling to her home planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] disguised as a refugee aboard the [[AA-9 Coruscant freighter/Legends|AA-9 Coruscant freighter]] [[Jendirian Valley/Legends|''Jendirian Valley'']], Naberrie, by then known as Padmé Amidala, remembered her [[Time/Legends|time]] on Shadda-Bi-Boran for the first time in years.<ref name="Junior">[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones'' junior novelization]]</ref> At her [[Naberrie family home|childhood home]] on Naboo, Amidala described the fate of Shadda-Bi-Boran to the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="AOTC novel" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|See that little one I'm holding? His name was N'a-kee-tula, which means "sweetheart." He was so full of life&mdash;all those kids were.|Padmé Amidala, explaining a holograph featuring her and N'a-kee-tula to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="AOTC novel" />}}
Shadda-Bi-Boran was inhabited by the [[Color/Legends|green]]-skinned Shadda-Bi-Borans, a primitive peaceful species that was governed by a [[Theocracy|theocratic]] sun [[Priest/Legends|priest]] caste. The Shadda-Bi-Borans comprised ninety-three percent of the population, with immigrated species making up the remaining seven percent. [[Shadda-Bi]] was the planet's native [[Language/Legends|language]], with [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] also being spoken there. The main export of Shadda-Bi-Boran was textiles, including Shadda silk, and the planet had no major imports.<ref name="TEA" /> During the Shadda-Bi-Boran exodus, Amidala met the Shadda-Bi-Boran [[Youngling/Legends|child]] [[N'a-kee-tula]] and recalled him and the other children as being full of life.<ref name="AOTC novel" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Pre-implosion, Shadda-Bi-Boran appears to have been a charming, happy world. Anything less just wouldn't provide the needed dose of pathos in light of its tragic destruction.|Daniel Wallace, commenting on Shadda-Bi-Boran in ''Star Wars Insider''|<ref name="Unseen" />}}
[[File:PadmeAnakinArtCritics-AotC.png|thumb|right|350px|Anakin Skywalker and Padmé Amidala discuss the latter's time on Shadda-Bi-Boran in a deleted scene.]]
Shadda-Bi-Boran was created for the backstory of Padmé Amidala for the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], written and directed by [[George Lucas]]. It was mentioned prominently in early versions of the script, but those mentions were reduced throughout the writing process. By the time the scene set in Amidala's childhood bedroom was filmed<ref name="Unseen">{{InsiderCite|80|The Unseen Planets of Episode II}}</ref> on [[August 25]], [[2000]],<ref name="Mythmaking">''[[Mythmaking: Behind the Scenes of Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> the dialogue that mentioned Shadda-Bi-Boran had been reduced to an indirect reference.<ref name="Unseen" />

The planet was first directly mentioned in the film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|novelization]] written by [[R. A. Salvatore]],<ref name="AOTC novel" /> and in the illustrated version of the film's screenplay included in ''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]'',<ref name="Art">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''</ref> both of which were published on [[April 23]], [[2002]].<ref name="Cargo Bay">{{RandomHouseOld|url=author/results.pperl?authorid=26771|text=R.A. Salvatore}}</ref><ref name="Art date">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/release/publish/news20020207.html|text=Book Preview: The Art of Episode II}}</ref> The scene in the film that mentioned the planet was ultimately [[Content cut from Star Wars|cut]] from the final release,<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> which premiered on [[May 16]], 2002.<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> The deleted scene was included on the DVD release of ''Attack of the Clones'', which launched on [[November 12]], 2002.<ref name="DVD">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/news/2002/08/news20020801.html|text=Episode II On DVD & VHS}}</ref>

The [[Star Wars Insider 80|eightieth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine,<ref name="Unseen" /> which began shipping to subscribers by [[January 14]], [[2005]] and to newsstands by [[January 31]],<ref name="Insider 80 Date">{{SWArchive|url=community/fanclub/mag/news20050110.html|text=Clone Wars Continue in ''Insider'' #80}}</ref> included the article "[[The Unseen Planets of Episode II]]" by [[Daniel Wallace]]. It discussed Shadda-Bi-Boran and its deletion from ''Attack of the Clones''. Wallace described the planet's name as sounding like a [[Wikipedia:Doo-wop|doo-wop]] lyric from the musical group [[Wikipedia:The Marcels|The Marcels]]. The article speculated that the planet had been a charming and pleasant place prior to its destruction and that it either became a lifeless husk or a shattered [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid field]]. Wallace suggested that the planet having anything other than a happy environment would not have led to an appropriately tragic impact.<ref name="Unseen" /> Shadda-Bi-Boran was first visually depicted in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by Wallace and [[Jason Fry]], which placed the planet in grid square O-18.<ref name="TEA" /> Fry expanded on the planet's tragic fate and described the [[galactic community]]'s efforts to save it in order to add depth to Amidala's backstory.<ref name="Endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_26.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 3 of 5)}}</ref>
